notes.ALB: Saze ensembles (clarinet, violin, llautë, def, accordion), çifteli/sharki, lahuta, fyell/kavall, cyla diare, zumare, surle+lodër, gajde; llautë coded shortneck; santur and darbuka judged marginal (0). Refs: Grove 'Albania', Wikipedia Music of Albania (from knowledge).
notes.BLR: Duda, lira, tsymbaly, skrypka, dudka, zhaleika, kuvikly, buben, baraban; balalaika/domra counted from folk use; dvoinitsa and gusli included as named folk instruments (moderate confidence). Refs: Grove 'Belarus', Wikipedia Music of Belarus.
notes.BOH: Moravian cimbalom bands, Bohemian/Chod dudy, dechovka brass, itinerant Bohemian harpists, citera, fujara, dvojačka, fanfrnoch, brumle, řehtačka; organ = Catholic liturgical + flašinet. Refs: Grove 'Czech Republic', Wikipedia Czech folk music.
notes.ESP: Gaita, zanfona, dulzaina/gralla, txistu+tamboril, alboka, trikitixa, rabel, guitar/bandurria/laúd, pandero, zambomba, castanets, knife-grinder panpipe; salterio/chicotén coded as dulcimer; Valencian village bandas give clarinet+brass. Refs: Grove 'Spain', Wikipedia Music of Spain.
notes.EST: Kannel, torupill, hiiu kannel (bowed lyre of Estonian Swedes/Vormsi, counted), parmupill, sarvepill/karjapasun, lõõtspill, Herrnhut brass choirs, Lutheran organ. Refs: Grove 'Estonia', Wikipedia Music of Estonia.
notes.HUN: String band (violin, brácsa, bass, gardon), cimbalom, citera, tekerő, duda, furulya, kettős furulya, tárogató/clarinet, koboz (Csángó), tambura (south), köcsögduda, doromb, kanna. Accordion and brass treated as non-core (0). Refs: Grove 'Hungary', Wikipedia Hungarian folk music.
notes.LIT: Kanklės, skudučiai (panpipe), lamzdeliai, birbynė, ragai/daudytės, dūdmaišis, cimbolai, armonika and bandonija (concertina), būgnas, tabalas; organ = Catholic liturgical. Refs: Grove 'Lithuania', Wikipedia Music of Lithuania.
notes.MAC: Zurla+tapan, gajda, kaval, šupelka, dvojanki, tambura, čalgija (violin, ut, kanun, santur, clarinet, tarabuka, def); brass and sax counted from village/Kočani brass bands and modern narodna practice. Refs: Grove 'Macedonia', Wikipedia Music of North Macedonia.
notes.MOL: Taraf (vioară, ţambal, cobză, contrabas, clarinet/taragot), nai, fluier, caval, cimpoi, bucium, fanfara brass, accordion, buhai, drâmbă, toacă, winter-custom bells; sax left 0. Refs: Grove 'Moldova', Wikipedia Music of Moldova.
notes.NGR: Fiddle/bass, Thuringian Waldzither, Blaskapelle (clarinet, brass), Spielmannszug fifes/drums/glockenspiel, East German Schalmeienkapelle, Sorbian dudy/Bock, hunting horn, accordion/Konzertina/bandoneon (Saxony), Leierkasten + Lutheran organ, Rummelpott. Harmonica (Klingenthal) excluded as manufacture only. Refs: Grove 'Germany: folk music', Wikipedia Music of Germany.
notes.NOR: Hardingfele/fiddle, langeleik, psalmodikon, seljefløyte, bukkehorn/lur, munnharpe, torader/trekkspill, Lutheran organ; school/korps brass excluded. Refs: Grove 'Norway', Wikipedia Music of Norway.
notes.NZL: Coded the settler (British/Irish) bush-band, pipe-band and brass-band tradition: fiddle, guitar/ukulele, tea-chest bass, whistle, pipes and pipe-band drums, brass bands, accordion, concertina, harmonica, bodhrán, spoons/lagerphone. Excluded Māori taonga pūoro as not widely played in shared traditional music. Refs: Te Ara, Wikipedia Music of New Zealand.
notes.POL: Kapela (skrzypce, basy, suka), cymbały, dudy/koza, lira korbowa, fujarka, ligawka/trombita, clarinet, village orkiestra dęta, harmonia/heligonka, bębenek, baraban, burczybas, diabelskie skrzypce, Catholic organ. Refs: Grove 'Poland', Wikipedia Polish folk music.
notes.POR: Gaita-de-foles, sanfona, rabeca, guitarra portuguesa/viola/cavaquinho/bandolim, pífaro, amolador panpipe, adufe, bombo/caixa (Zés-Pereiras), sarronca, ferrinhos/reco-reco, bandas filarmónicas (clarinet, brass); Portuguese 'concertina' is a diatonic accordion. Refs: Grove 'Portugal', Wikipedia Music of Portugal.
notes.QUE: Coded the French-Canadian settler tradition: fiddle, accordion, harmonica, guimbarde, spoons/bones/podorythmie, guitar, piano accompaniment, Catholic organ. First Nations instruments excluded as not widely played in shared trad; flute left 0. Refs: Canadian Encyclopedia 'Folk music, Franco-Canadian', Wikipedia Music of Quebec.
notes.ROM: Taraf (vioară, ceteră, contrabas, ţambal, cobză), nai, fluier/caval/tilincă, fluier gemănat, clarinet/taragot, Banat saxophone, fanfare, cimpoi, bucium, buhai, drâmbă, toacă, plugușor bells. Refs: Grove 'Romania', Wikipedia Music of Romania.
notes.SCO: Fiddle, Highland and Lowland pipes, clàrsach, whistle, pipe-band drums, Scottish dance band (accordion, piano, drums), moothie, trump; organ 0 (Presbyterian), guitar/bodhrán treated as revival-era. Refs: Grove 'Scotland', Wikipedia Music of Scotland.
notes.UKR: Troista muzyka (skrypka, tsymbaly, buben/baraban), lira of the lirnyky, kobza/bandura, sopilka, kuvytsi, dvodentsivka, zhalomiika, buhai, accordion/bayan; trembita, drymba and koza left 0 as Carpathian (excluded region). Refs: Grove 'Ukraine', Wikipedia Music of Ukraine.
